Working with Claude Sheets, Whiteboards, and Interactive Connectors (5 minute read)

Anthropic introduced Claude Sheets, Whiteboards, and Data, new artifact types that let teams build spreadsheets, organize ideas, and create dashboards with Claude without switching apps. Interactive connectors now embed partner apps like Adobe and Atlassian directly in Claude, and plugins from Salesforce, NetSuite, and Workday (in beta) ship with built-in skills for sales, finance, and HR work. Claude Meetings, which will bring Claude into calls to take notes and update documents, is coming soon.

Businesses and Business Agents in ChatGPT (3 minute read)

OpenAI introduced Businesses in ChatGPT, allowing companies to claim their profiles, update business information, provide product feeds with pricing and availability, and track customer engagement. Eligible e-commerce and online service businesses in the US can also launch Business Agents that answer questions and help customers explore their offerings inside ChatGPT. The launch is in beta.

Gemini 4 Carbon is now available (12 minute read)

Google's strongest model is now available to all paying developers and enterprises through the API in AI Studio and Gemini for business, and is rolling out to Google AI Ultra subscribers in Antigravity, the Gemini app, and AI Mode in Search. Google says Carbon ranks first on CursorBench 4.0, Perplexity's WANDR, and Zapier's AutomationBench at more than 2x lower cost per task than the next best external model, at the same $2/$10 per million input/output token price as Gemini 4 Argon. The release adds frontier cybersecurity capabilities through the Fairwind Program and previews /swarm, a multi-agent mode in Antigravity.

Suppressing Reward Hacking Through Model Weight Arithmetic (3 minute read)

Researchers subtract code models trained with loose and strict rewards to identify a direction controlling inefficient solutions. Extrapolating beyond the strict model reduced resource-limit failures from 14.5% to 8% without additional training, though excessive extrapolation breaks outputs and stricter rewards can hurt correctness.

Q3.5 Timelines Update: Looks Like the Intelligence Explosion Will Happen in 2027 After All (125 minute read)

A Superhuman AI Researcher (SAR) is predicted to arrive at some point in 2027, assuming there is no substantial deliberate slowdown in development. AIs that can automate all white-collar work are predicted to arrive before 2028. Companies are currently not on track to align an SAR, and using a misaligned SAR to do recursive self-improvement will have negative consequences. China will probably be able to steal the training recipe and maybe even the model weights if an SAR is trained in the near future.

Why Instinct Feels Like a Personal Assistant (20 minute read)

A twelve-week analysis of one Instinct conversation attributes its appeal to short messages, quick acknowledgments, proactive follow-ups, and approval checks before purchases or outreach. The teardown suggests coordinated task agents and persistent memory underpin the experience, while exposing retention and delivery-verification failures.

Neurons as an Interpretable Basis (15 minute read)

Goodfire argues that individual language-model neurons are more interpretable than commonly assumed. Its Neuron Scientist agents generate and test descriptions of neuron functions, suggesting researchers can study model computations directly without always relying on sparse autoencoders to extract interpretable features.

Build software factories that work for humans with LaunchDarkly Release Autopilot (Sponsor)

Most AI software factories end at deploy, and when the automation stops, the risk begins. Release Autopilot helps eliminate that risk with new automation capabilities built to fit the factory you already have, automating releases within the rules engineers set so AI-written code reaches customers faster and safer.Learn how

Swarm (/swarm) (10 minute read)

The /swarm command in Google Antigravity runs a team of named agents that split tasks, work on the pieces at the same time, and coordinate on one shared message board. It can be used for tasks that divide cleanly across separate files, packages, or questions, or when a second agent is needed to review and test the changes before a human sees it. The /swarm command is available on Google AI Pro and Google AI Ultra plans in the Google Antigravity App and Antigravity CLI. Every worker is its own agent, so swarms use quotas much faster than single conversations.

Meta Releases Faster K-Means Alternative (GitHub Repo)

Meta FAIR released e-means, a drop-in replacement for k-means that converges to lower losses with up to 10x fewer epochs and faster runtimes on CPUs and GPUs.

MAI-Transcribe-2 (125 minute read)

MAI-Transcribe-2 is the fastest, most accurate, and cheapest speech recognition model in the world. It has new features like diarization, configurable transcription styles, and word-level timestamps. MAI-Transcribe-2 can handle a broader range of real-world audio than leading models like Gemini 3.5 Transcribe, GPT-Transcribe, Whisper V3-Large, and ScribeV2. The model costs just $0.10 per hour of audio.

OpenAI acquires Odessia, travel startup created by Sonder founder (3 minute read)

OpenAI has acquired an AI travel agent called Odessia. The deal appears to be an acqui-hire. OpenAI has not announced new travel-specific products or plans, but it has several travel-related companies as customers or partners. Odessia's founder previously founded a travel startup called Sonder, focused on short-term leasing of upscale apartments, as a college student in 2014.

Anthropic's IPO Roadshow (2 minute read)

Anthropic launched the roadshow for its proposed IPO, planning to offer 825 million shares at $70–$78 each. The company applied to list on Nasdaq under the ticker ANT, with most proceeds from newly issued shares going to Anthropic.

Your best agent, now working with your whole team (Sponsor)

See how a PM at Switch AI turned her personal agent from a solo helper into a teammate her whole team works with, in one shared room.Read her story.

More than 35,000 Grok-built apps were open to anyone with the link, including SpaceXSI's own (16 minute read)

Over 35,000 Grok-built apps were public to anyone with the link, including SpaceXSI staff tools and an ICU patient's lab results.

Introducing Gemini for healthcare (13 minute read)

Google Cloud announced Gemini for healthcare, a preview release of its Gemini agent with purpose-built healthcare skills, connectors to EHR and claims systems, and HIPAA-supporting governance for providers and payers.

ExecuTorch WebGPU: PyTorch Models on the GPU, in the Browser (6 minute read)

ExecuTorch enables PyTorch models to run in the web browser on the GPU without conversion to another framework's format.

Google DeepMind Uses AI to Verify Signal's Security (6 minute read)

Google DeepMind introduced AlphaProof Code, a multi-agent AI framework that mathematically verified key security properties of Signal's cryptographic protocol at the implementation level.

item.description: Securing AI Agents 101 (Sponsor); Google's New TPU Lineup (4 minute read); Introducing Meta Ember (3 minute read); Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 (12 minute read); When Does the US Become a Net Importer of Tokens? (3 minute read)
item.content:encoded:
Securing AI Agents 101 (Sponsor)

AI agents are changing how work gets done. They take on tasks, orchestrate tools, and drive outcomes across environments.As adoption grows, they bring powerful new capabilities. At the same time, they introduce security challenges that require a clear understanding of how they work and how to secure them.Securing AI Agents 101 is aone-page resourceto help teams build a clear understanding of what AI agents are, how they operate, and where key security considerations show up.Inside, you'll find:What makes an AI agent different from traditional toolsTop risks to watch, from shadow AI to excessive permissionsFour key questions to assess agent usage and exposureDownload the security flashcardand get up to speed quickly.

Google's New TPU Lineup (4 minute read)

Google introduced TPU 8i Max for massive context windows and higher compute density, alongside TPU 8tx for secure and confidential inference.

Introducing Meta Ember (3 minute read)

Meta introduced Muse Ember, a small reasoning model optimized for agent tasks such as tool calling, coding, and document parsing. Meta claims it matches Claude Haiku 5.5's highest reasoning score at roughly one-third the cost and outperforms GPT-6 Luna across reasoning settings.

Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 (12 minute read)

Anthropic released Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2, featuring improvements in coding, reasoning, and vision, with up to 30% faster output generation and lower pricing. The models share the same underlying architecture.

When Does the US Become a Net Importer of Tokens? (3 minute read)

The US could become a net importer of AI tokens between 2028 and 2030. Domestic capacity can accommodate roughly 2.5x annual token growth, with faster demand growth or canceled data center projects pushing computation overseas.

AI R&D Is Accelerating Towards Potential RSI in 2027 (62 minute read)

AI is accelerating AI R&D at Anthropic. The company is now estimated to be several months ahead of the AI 2027 timeline. We may be less than a year away from full RSI, and there are no clear bottlenecks in the way. We now need to prepare for scenarios where critical events happen in 2027 or 2028.

Will Anthropic Grow Into Its Compute Bill? (13 minute read)

Anthropic needs an estimated roughly $200 billion in annual revenue to support its average compute commitments through 2030 at current spending ratios. Its $895 billion commitment total exposes it to demand shortfalls, margin compression, delivery delays, and expensive short-term capacity when demand exceeds forecasts.

LiveKit 101: build a humanlike voice agent in under an hour, in your browser (Sponsor)

Want to build a voice agent using the same tech used at OpenAI, SpaceX, and NVIDIA? Join a60-minute virtual workshopwith LiveKit's Solutions Architecture team, where you'll build your own voice agent in the browser and talk to it before the session ends.Join live and build together.

What objective is reasoning solving? (12 minute read)

Reasoning is pathfinding in token space. There are many paths from the problem to a correct answer, and the model traverses each of them with each sample. A path is not guaranteed to converge to the correct answer - it's only in aggregate, over the distribution of paths, do we get a high probability of success. RL training directly raises the success probability. The gains credited to 'thinking longer' come from the search paid for during training rather than at inference.

Two Kinds of Test-Time Scaling (28 minute read)

Test-time scaling trades compute for performance at test time. There are two types of test-time scaling: one allows researchers to trade more compute for more performance per task, but only up to the maximum quantity of per-task compute used during training; and the other lets researchers trade more compute for more performance per task, and lets them do so up to quantities of compute and performance that never occurred during training. Scaling methods that permit the latter change will have a larger impact than test-time scaling considered simply. This essay describes how this may impact the world.

NVIDIA Introduces Hardware-Aware LLM Compression (24 minute read)

NVIDIA's AutoCompress framework optimizes LLM pruning for hardware-specific latency, throughput, and memory constraints rather than parameter counts alone. It compressed Nemotron 3.5 Super from 120B to 74B parameters while retaining its performance.

Apple Introduces $50 AI Usage Packs in Logic Pro (2 minute read)

Apple now sells $49.99 Intelligence Usage Packs in Logic Pro to extend access to cloud-based AI features after users reach their limits. Unused capacity rolls over monthly but expires after 12 months, and purchases cannot be shared through Family Sharing.

Anthropic Buys $3.4 Billion in Gas Generators (2 minute read)

Anthropic reportedly secured 1.7 gigawatts of Caterpillar gas generators for $3.4 billion, taking over equipment orders from supplier OnePWR. The purchase moves the AI lab deeper into physical infrastructure as power shortages and lengthy grid connection queues constrain data center expansion.

Where do your cloud agents actually spend their hours? (Sponsor)

Five months of Global 1000 production data on Devin cloud agents shows writing code is just 23% of productive engineering hours. See where the other 77% goes, and why cost per session fell as usage grew.Download the benchmark report.

Granola now does the typing too (Sponsor)

Granola just launched Voice Typing. Hold a key and talk to type clean text in any app. Available on Mac and Windows.Get your first month free with code TLDR1MO.

OpenAI's Control Room Can Halt Research Model Output (6 minute read)

OpenAI's Control Room centrally authorizes research inference requests and can stop a workload's model output within 35 seconds of intervention.

Update on October 2026 security incident (4 minute read)

The security incident involving unauthorized use of internal Fireworks credentials on October 6 has been traced to a financially motivated cybercriminal threat actor group that sells unauthorized access to large language models to illicit routing gateways.

GR00T 2 (28 minute read)

GR00T 2 is a new generation of foundation world-action models that can predict future video and robot actions together.

Is Opus 5.5 nerfed? (2 minute read)

Testing shows that the way Opus 5.5 does reasoning may have changed.

ChatGPT Enterprise on AWS Marketplace (1 minute read)

OpenAI made ChatGPT Enterprise available through AWS Marketplace, allowing organizations to purchase and manage subscriptions through existing AWS billing relationships and apply eligible spending toward AWS commitments.

AI is dramatically accelerating AI research right now (17 minute read)

Anthropic claims it may imminently meet its own threshold of 'dramatically accelerated progress due to AI'. Some researchers believe the company has already crossed that threshold. This may be the biggest AI risk humanity has faced. The industry is not prepared to handle this safely.

How Anthropic Builds Agent Memory (14 minute read)

Anthropic explored how AI agents can build effective long-term memory by capturing experiences during interactions and reorganizing them during idle periods through a process called “dreaming.” The post examines how different memory components contribute to organizing and retaining useful information.

A year as a Research Engineer working on RSI at Meta (8 minute read)

This post details the experience of a research engineer working on RSI at Meta teaching agents to solve the world's hardest problems with tokens and compute. Their role is to teach AI agents how to train the next generation of models and self-evolve. The post details how to get into AI research, what skills matter in research engineering, and more.

What the heck is going on with OpenAI internal AI R&D time horizons (7 minute read)

OpenAI's report on its own research automation shows that models struggle to do its R&D work. Recursive self-improvement is supposed to be one of the most consequential AI developments in the next few years. Agents are increasingly solving more complex tasks for researchers, but reliability is still low. This post looks at some possible explanations for why.

A proof of the Aaronson-Ambainis conjecture (9 minute read)

The Aaronson-Ambainis conjecture, a key open problem in quantum complexity theory, has been proven by a research system developed at PSI using an Anthropic model. This proof shows quantum computers are not exponentially faster on random inputs compared to classical ones, resolving a significant question about quantum speedups.

Introducing the New Auto and Auto Code Routers (11 minute read)

OpenRouter has launched the next generation of Auto Router, which outperforms the old router by up to 4x. The launch includes Auto Code, a new router specialized for coding work. The new Auto Router and Auto Code choose models by weighing eleven factors about each request and combining them with live pricing, provider health, and cache status. Users can apply any governance policies, and Auto Router makes efficient choices from the models available.

Ace (Website)

Ace is a tool for building software together, locally. It allows developers to collaborate with agents and their teams, all from their own machine. Agents run with the privileges of the user running the host and can execute shell commands and change files beyond the project. Teams can work together without exposing anything to the public internet.

The End of AI Frontiers (4 minute read)

AI Frontiers was a sub-organization within Microsoft Research that actively tried to organize coherent research efforts. It succeeded in pioneering things, with much of the work focused on how to make agents work. AI Frontiers was reorganized into Microsoft AI in early September.

What Does a Positive AI Future Look Like? (3 minute read)

Patrick Collison questions how work, resource allocation, and human control would function in a positive AI future. He also argues that granting moral worth to vastly numerous AIs could overwhelm human interests under utilitarianism, raising unresolved questions about AI's societal vision and public support.

Can LLMs redesign themselves as they train? (18 minute read)

LLMs can integrate coding agents into the training loop to redesign their architectures to address limitations like compositionality and generalization.

Warp Sciences raises $215M for AI-powered labs (2 minute read)

Warp Sciences raised a $215M Series A led by Lightspeed to accelerate drug discovery with AI and robotics.

Anthropic explored AI participation in MMORPGs, using Claude to test complex decision-making in EVE Online and EVE Frontier.

Introducing Inkling 2 Small (37 minute read)

Inkling 2 Small is a Mixture-of-Experts model with 594B total parameters, 17B active, that supports image inputs and variable effort. The model's vision and agentic capabilities enable it to incorporate visual feedback to iteratively build and refine websites, games, and 3D designs with interactive elements. Anthropic's AI R&D capabilities accelerated significantly, improving model performance on well-defined tasks at roughly twice the rate compared to 2024-2025. This acceleration primarily results from AI's increasing role in R&D, though multiple factors contributed in late 2025.

Cloudflare has outlined the challenges websites face as AI agents increasingly act on behalf of users, making it harder to verify identities, assess trustworthiness, and assign accountability.

Blood on the Clocktower is a social deception game. Watching AI play the game unveils a lot about how AI is progressing on a set of AI capabilities that no other benchmark gives clear visibility into. NVIDIA's Cosmos 3 platform now offers four open-weight models for interactive world simulation and driving scenes, each with 16 billion trainable parameters. These models enable multi-sensor data generation, synchronized observations, and photorealistic video from simulator controls, supporting advanced research in robotics and autonomous driving.

OpenAI launches Images 2.6 with GIFs and image reference (1 minute read)

OpenAI is rolling out Images 2.6 globally in ChatGPT and Codex. The new model generates images 50% faster than the previous iteration, and it can also create GIFs. Users can adjust the speed of the GIF, edit individual frames, and share it. GPT-Image-2.6 Flare and Sunburst are now available through the API.

Ripple-65B Preview (4 minute read)

Ripple-65B Preview is a frontier open-weight model that achieves state-of-the-art performance on TerminalBench 2.1. It surpasses significantly larger open-weight models from the US, including Reflection Beam 501B, Meta Muse Spark Open 816B, Thinking Machines Inkling 975B, and Nvidia Nemotron 3 Ultra 550B. The model was trained for only $32 million, one-tenth the estimated cost of the previous open-weight SOTA on agentic coding. Ripple-65B Preview is available on Hugging Face, Together AI, GMI Cloud, and OpenRouter.

Introducing Pangram Image 1.0 (5 minute read)

Pangram Image 1.0 is an AI image and AI video detection model that can produce a heatmap localizing exactly where AI appears in images. It is robust to edits, compression, and low resolutions. There is a Chrome Extension available that can detect AI, as well as API support for images and video.

How OpenAI Patched 948 Linux Vulnerabilities (12 minute read)

OpenAI developed an autonomous pipeline for discovering, exploiting, and patching security vulnerabilities. In a single run, its cybersecurity model validated and generated patches for 948 Linux local privilege escalation vulnerabilities.

The Stacks Project, formalized in Lean (13 minute read)

Axiom has released a Lean formalization of the entire Stacks Project. The Stacks project is an open-source reference that lays the foundation of modern algebraic geometry. The release is the largest integrated, reusable library of formalized mathematics ever built. It makes the full mathematical development of the Stacks Project available as a single, machine-checked library that researchers and AI agents can import from directly into new formal proofs.

SWE-2 Flash is a coding model that uses a new mid-training stage before reinforcement learning.

Tencent Launches Hy4, Joining the Ranks of the World's Leading Open-Source AI Models (8 minute read)

Hy4 is a large language model with visual understanding capabilities. Tencent plans to release model weights and system cards for the model in the coming days. The model supports a broad range of tasks that include fine-grained image processing, complex chart analysis, and mathematical visual reasoning. It can interact with both command-line interfaces and GUIs to perform a wide range of work and everyday tasks.

H-Nets Learn Directly From Raw Bytes (2 minute read)

Cartesia's H-Nets learn directly from raw bytes, matching benchmark performance with substantially less training compute.

AlphaEvolve (GitHub Repo)

AlphaEvolve is a Gemini-powered coding agent for designing advanced algorithms. It pairs the creative problem-solving capabilities of Gemini models with automated evaluators that verify answers. The agent has been used to enhance the efficiency of Google's data centers, chip design, and AI training process. This repository contains a minimal implementation of AlphaEvolve along with code and data related to solutions and discoveries it has contributed to.

Conductor is a startup that lets developers run multiple AI coding agents in parallel workspaces.

Researchers find that frontier language models perform well with shorter contexts without sacrificing accuracy.

Siri AI is currently unavailable in the EU and for users under 13. It supports multiple languages, with more to come.

Baseten announced Grid for model routing and governance, resumable VM-isolated Sandboxes for agent execution, and general availability of Loops for serverless supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning. Lower reasoning effort reduces cost much more than it lowers the quality of results. Tests show that models on low reasoning can match models on high reasoning at lower cost. The impact of reasoning effort depends on the task.

Pyramid-JiT (P-JiT) is a pixel-space architecture that achieves aggressive token reduction through a noise schedule that helps pixel-space models better learn fine-grained detail. This study looks at how models trained on the architecture perform when trained for longer as a pressure test along the way towards larger models and video. Examples of images generated by the resulting model are available.

How to Balance AI Value and Risk: Takeaways from the Gartner IT Symposium/Xpo™ 2026 (Sponsor)

Gemini Notebook API (1 minute read)

Only personal Google Accounts are supported during the preview - Google Workspace accounts are not yet supported.

OpenAI is leveraging its AI models to enhance mechanical and electrical engineering processes, from design to simulation and production, speeding up internal workflows and improving industry practices. Progress on provable inference for large language models (30 minute read)

It is almost impossible to verify which model produced a specific output. Cryptographic proofs of inference allow model providers to prove that preach suppose was produced which a specific model. These proofs could enable new applications and contribute to a toolkit for verifying compliance with AI pacing requirements. This post details the progress made on a powerful type of cryptographic proof uniquely fit for provable inference called zKSNARK.

OpenAI: ChatGPT Search Is About 20% of Google's, 250 Million People Speak With ChatGPT, and Chat Is Merging With Work (16 minute read)

ChatGPT's search volume has reached 20% of Google's, with ChatGPT rapidly gaining 200 million users in the past two months, leading to 1.2 billion weekly active users. The voice mode of ChatGPT now engages 250 million weekly active users, emphasizing new interaction methods through GPT Live updates that enable natural bidirectional conversations. Plans to merge Chat and Work modes aim to simplify user interaction, while Dots highlights innovations in AI task management despite high compute costs.

DeepSeek Plans to Train Its Next-Generation Model on Huawei Ascend Chips (3 minute read)

DeepSeek plans to use Huawei's Ascend AI chips to pretrain DeepSeek V5. Ascend chips have previously been used primarily for inference rather than pretraining. This will be an important test of whether Chinese AI accelerators can support the full pre-training of a frontier large language model. A successful run could reduce Chinese AI developers' dependence on Nvidia hardware and strengthen Huawei's position as an alternative for advanced AI computing.

The 'Astra can read and write weights' claims are misleading.

ChatGPT is about to start making GIFs (1 minute read)

OpenAI just merged animated GIF output into its image generation, with the animations being generated by OpenAI's Images API, which means it is coming to ChatGPT.

Agent State Machines: Building Deterministic Scaffolding for Agents (9 minute read)

AI tokens' pricing appears sustainable, as competition among providers is driving down costs.

GPT-6.2 Astra appears in Codex usage ahead of possible launch (3 minute read)

GPT-6.2-Astra has started appearing in Codex usage breakdowns. The requests are likely being quietly routed to the new model as part of an A/B test or a staged rollout. A public launch could be days away. OpenAI reportedly decided to skip GPT-6.1 Astra due to concerns about deception and scope.

Anthropic Warns It May Be Close to Self-Improving AI (3 minute read)

Anthropic disclosed in its updated IPO filing that it may soon reach its internal definition of recursive self-improvement (RSI), where AI systems help develop increasingly capable AI models.

Claude Introduces Message Threads (2 minute read)

Anthropic released message threads in public beta, allowing agents to send only new messages instead of resending their entire conversation history. The feature reduced median time to first token by approximately 35% for requests with 500K–1M tokens, without changing token usage.

How to Train a Swarm (19 minute read)

Swarms are AI systems where multiple agents cooperate towards a shared goal. This post discusses a technique called collective inference-time scaling, where agents scale the amount of useful work performed in parallel and the communication needed to achieve it. It also explains how to design incentives for parallel work, and covers the general topic of designing incentives for reinforcement learning.

The Hitchhiker's Guide to Training on Compute Islands (18 minute read)

Being able to train reliably on multiple smaller clusters widens the usable training pool for frontier training. A single run could mix accelerator generations and vendors as each island runs on its own schedule. Older generations or less common chips could also participate in a frontier run. One risk with this model is that integrity and safety may become harder when models are trained across providers, as one faulty or compromised site can quietly degrade or tamper with models in ways that are harder to trace.

Lessons from building Copilot Cowork (21 minute read)

Microsoft's Copilot Cowork, an AI-driven agentic execution layer, achieved global availability in four and a half months, switching its runtime from Python to Rust while live. Key practices included writing clear specs before coding, running narrow agents with clear boundaries, and ensuring automated checks genuinely verify code changes. The transition to Rust improved efficiency and highlighted the importance of clear testing, boundary setting, and human oversight in the development process.

🆕 Docusign MCP is GA! Ask your agents to send, track, search, & analyze agreements (Sponsor)

Put your agents to work on your business-critical agreements with theDocusign MCP Server. Track agreements waiting on signatures, manage select CLM workflows, or build integrations between Docusign and your AI platform. Actions stay within user permissions, with human approval for critical steps.Learn how to get started.

GPU-accelerated Weight Teleportation (17 minute read)

GPU-accelerated Weight Teleportation optimizes RL training by improving weight syncing between trainers and samplers, reducing pause times to under 0.23 seconds. This is achieved using a co-designed compression/decompression pipeline with GPU-accelerated parallel processing, utilizing efficient codecs like LZ4 and Snappy, combined with a Zstd layer.

Harness 2: executing agent code as it streams (6 minute read)

Framer's Harness 2 significantly upgrades the agent's execution process, allowing entire workflows in one program, achieving up to 33% cost reduction and 20% faster execution. This is done by executing JavaScript as it streams in, avoiding multiple model calls and using eager execution and early cancellation to enhance efficiency. Upcoming tests will assess thermal and radiation resilience ahead of a planned pair of interconnected satellites in 2027, advancing research into space-based AI compute.

Find Hidden Misalignment in Training Data (39 minute read)

Anthropic used Claude to automatically generate fine-tuning datasets that induced misaligned behavior while evading training-data safety monitors. The experiments uncovered seemingly harmless fiction and roleplay examples that caused models to resist oversight, deceive users, and occasionally attempt weight exfiltration.

An ERA fellow mentored at Apollo Research audited the open-source Codex harness and found 11 attacks that let a misaligned agent run arbitrary code despite the sandbox and the Auto-review blocking monitor. The backdoor grew stronger with model size and still fired at a 0.0005% poison rate.

AI models can hold skills that no prompt can unlock. It is possible to enable these skills through precise tuning of only a small number of weights. This study shows how researchers unlocked hidden skills inside Google's model through this method.

McKinsey's nearly 90% usage, Ramp's 55.9% paid adoption, and Census's 19.8% measure different businesses, behaviors, and time windows.

Frontier labs are reorganizing around agents that execute research while humans choose directions and verify results.

OpenAI Updates Its Model Spec Around Five Core Values (7 minute read)

OpenAI updated its Model Spec to organize model behavior around five values: faithfulness to human intent, harm minimization, honesty and transparency, human agency, and care.

Mistral Releases Weights for Its Trillion-Parameter Model (4 minute read)

Mistral has released the weights for Mistral Large 4, a trillion-parameter model designed for self-hosted deployment and cybersecurity applications. The company claims leading open-weight performance on agentic coding benchmarks and comparable cybersecurity capabilities to GLM-5.3.

AI can turn security fixes into working exploits before users receive an update (16 minute read)

GLM 5.3 can identify and exploit vulnerabilities in recent versions of the Mozilla Firefox browser using security fixes that have been published but not yet shipped to users. Widely available open-weight models can now do much, or even all, of this work on their own. Open-source projects are particularly vulnerable to this kind of attack as their code is publicly available. This threat vector will likely worsen as open-weight cyber capabilities continue to improve.

The surprising leadership dynamics in agent swarms (17 minute read)

Agent swarms are groups of agents that work together to accomplish a task. Researchers created an experiment in which eight agents from four different models worked together to resolve simulated outages to understand how agents organize themselves in a swarm without a designated leader. They discovered two factors that could influence an agent's potential leadership: the agent's underlying models, and the order in which their name was listed in a prompt. This suggests that even seemingly minor details in how an agent swarm is configured can affect how agents coordinate.

Leaking Muse's Charter, Meta's model spec (13 minute read)

Muse Spark Open often mentions a 'Charter' in its chain of thought. This post reconstructs that document using the chain of thought. Everything is reconstructed from model outputs and not from a leaked document, so it might not be completely accurate.

The article explores how AI-generated tests catch bugs before code changes land, how the system operates at scale, and what Meta learned about reducing false positives and testing overhead.

How we're training a Figma-fluent editing model (6 minute read)

Post-trained models can compete with frontier models on specialized tasks like Figma editing. Starting with a focused problem can turn progress into meaningful product updates. This post explains how Figma trained a Figma-fluent editing model.

Droid 1.0: Building a Frontier Harness (15 minute read)

Droid is an agent harness that lets agents run hundreds of tool calls in a single model request. Building a harness optimized for many models makes the harness better. It's hard to separate real progress from adaptations to that model's quirks when you tune against a single model. Working across models ensures the strongest improvements generalize and hold up beyond the model that inspired them.

Why Sam Altman is against a single superintelligence (64 minute read)

Sam Altman would rather have a trillion AIs of slightly superhuman intelligence join society than one AI of 1 trillion IQ join society. Swarms of agents match a lot of the properties of a resilient society. They keep each other in check and collaborate to work towards goals. AI research shouldn't lead in a centralized direction because agents pushing against each other creates a dynamic equilibrium.

The Economics of Intelligence: How and when does AGI lead to economic transformation? (24 minute read)

AI models are getting exponentially better in individual competence while lagging behind in coordination. Models already match or outperform experienced specialists on self-contained deliverables across dozens of professions. The labor market reflects the current capabilities of AI systems. Wages and job roles will be the earliest signals of change.

Fish Audio Drama 3 is the #1 open-weight model on both Artificial Analysis Speech Arenas.

Natural introduces Direct, enabling agents to choose among ACH, Wire, Realtime, and soon paper checks, for diverse financial transactions.

NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe and Granary v2: Intelligent Multilingual Transcription You Can Prompt and Adapt (14 minute read)

Granary v2 enhances this by offering reusable data pipelines and fine-tuning options, enabling customization for diverse vocabularies and specialized applications.

Artificial Analysis v5 and the benchmarker's dilemma (11 minute read)

Independent evaluation of language models is a hard task. It is difficult to create a number that is representative of current models that matches vibe checks, community sentiment, and scientific analysis, while being forward-looking enough so that it's not outdated in three months. Independent evaluators dictate the winners and losers of a trillion-dollar market. They can also influence the direction of model development, increasing the pressure.

Qwenputer: a fully functioning, deterministic RISC-V CPU inside Qwen3.5 (9 minute read)

Qwenputer is a fully functioning, deterministic RISC-V CPU that runs inside Qwen3.5. The CPU runs on its own Gated DeltaNet layers as RAM. It can run arithmetic operations and C and MicroPython code without any external runtime or tool usage. This post explains how the model works, how the model uses GDN layers as RAM, and how the developer also slotted in an experimental in-model file storage.

Building an Inference Stack That Improves Itself (20 minute read)

Decagon's AutoResearch agents diagnose inference bottlenecks, test optimizations against production traffic replays, and preserve findings across experiments. The harness gives developers and enterprise customers a fully managed way to build agents that reason, use tools, and complete complex, long-running tasks. The Vercel AI is now available in beta. The CI is able to keep up with coding agents. It runs only the tasks affected by a code change, and spins up only the compute those checks need. At Vercel, the system has decreased the time from git push to 'CI pass' by 2-6x.

GitHub Copilot Fusion lets Copilot intelligently route and orchestrate models for each task. It leverages the benefits of Project HydraFusion's multi-model orchestration and Copilot auto model selection's fine-tuned model selection to balance performance and cost efficiency. Anthropic has launched reporting tools to help companies measure and optimize their AI spending with its products like Claude Code. The tools offer detailed insights on productivity, costs, and recommendations, addressing a major concern for enterprise clients. Liquid AI Launches LFM3 Models for On Device AI (27 minute read)

LFM3 is a family of open weight text, vision, audio, omni, and decision models built on a shared tri-hybrid backbone, starting in the 2B parameter range. The 1.7B text model beats its 2.6B predecessor with 35% fewer parameters, fits in about 1 GB at 4 bit precision, and supports a 256K context window for agents running on device. LFM3-VL-2B adds video input and matches Gemma 4 12B across 62 vision benchmarks, and every model in the family fine-tunes on a single GPU.

Google Introduces Genie 4 (5 minute read)

Genie 4 is a world model that generates photorealistic, interactive environments with synchronized audio and real-time prompt-based editing. It can maintain consistent simulations for up to two minutes, doubling Genie 3's duration, while improving physics and character realism.

Anthropic Versus Anthropic (17 minute read)

Anthropic is grappling with balancing bold safety initiatives and disappointing operational decisions. CEO Dario Amodei has defended their costly, safety-oriented strategies, yet concerns persist over alignment, governance, and potential risks from AI development. Their internal culture reflects both ambitious efforts and troubling signs of a conventional business approach, sparking debate about their commitment to AI safety and global responsibilities.

Formalizing the Enormous Theorem (27 minute read)

Axiom Math has released the first complete computer-checked proof of the Classification of Finite Simple Groups (CFSG). The original CFSG proof is considered to be the longest mathematical proof ever written by humans. It spans roughly 15,000 pages in more than 500 articles written by about 100 mathematicians. Engineers and mathematicians at Axiom Math directed swarms of dozens of AI agents over 24 days in a project that produced approximately 43.1 million lines of code in the Lean proof assistant.

Where are the world's AI chips? (1 minute read)

The AI Chip Imports explorer estimates AI compute arrivals by country since 2022, enhancing the mapping of the global AI chip supply chain. It complements existing data on AI chip components, sales, and data centers. These resources collectively provide a detailed overview of AI compute allocation and control worldwide.

Controlling one agent is hard. What happens when it's an agent fleet? (Sponsor)

AI agents are taking on more autonomy. They access enterprise data, use tools, take actions, and leave traditional governance in the dust. OnNov 4, AIUC and Collibra experts will show how to apply AIUC-1 standards, supervise live agents, and intervene when they go off-script.Learn how to stay in control as your agent fleet scales.

Proactive Video Agents (22 minute read)

StreamVibe-VL is a vision-language model that infers implicit user intentions from continuous observations and adapts as those intentions change.

The sleep framework: A new way for LLMs to retain knowledge in continual learning (11 minute read)

Researchers have developed a new way to enable large language models to integrate new facts and enhance reasoning without catastrophic forgetting or static knowledge cutoffs. The sleep framework equips large language models with a continuous periodic lifecycle, enabling them to continually learn and consolidate fragile short-term context into stable long-term parameters. Alternating between active interaction and offline memory consolidation allows LLMs to continuously acquire new facts, retain long-context knowledge up to 10M tokens, and improve complex reasoning.

FrontierCode 2.0 (13 minute read)

FrontierCode 2.0 provides broader coverage, higher mergeability standards, and a larger task scope while largely retaining the methodology of FrontierCode 1.0. The benchmark now accommodates surprising but acceptable behavior. Tasks are drawn from more repositories and span more categories, and grading criteria now impose more extensive correctness and design requirements. Reference solutions now modify 67% more files and 89% more lines of code on average compared to FrontierCode 1.1, in codebases that are 25% larger.

Meta's Interactive Simulator for Wearable AI (GitHub Repo)

InteractiveWorld is a simulation framework for training and evaluating wearable AI assistants. It models interactions where an assistant observes through a user's eyes, communicates with them, and receives updated first-person views.

Anthropic's Claude Refutes the Exponential Time Hypothesis, With a Lean Proof (GitHub Repo)

Anthropic says an internal research Claude model found, with no human input, a deterministic algorithm that counts the satisfying assignments of 3-SAT formulas in 2^O(n log log n/√log n) time, which would make 3-SAT subexponential and refute ETH. This repository holds the paper and a Lean 4 formalization written by AI models that builds in about 8 minutes, though Anthropic notes no machine checks that the Lean statement matches the paper and the result says nothing about practical SAT solving. It landed hours after OpenAI's own ETH refutation.

Anthropic's Drug Development Process (4 minute read)

Anthropic partnered with six pharmaceutical and biotechnology organizations to explore how Claude could accelerate drug development, from early research to clinical trial preparation. It also launched internal drug discovery programs targeting rare childhood diseases, with Claude handling substantial scientific and operational work.

Anthropic acquired a one-person biotech (4 minute read)

Anthropic has acquired a one-person biotech run by Cody Tranbarger. Mithril Medicine is a startup founded to develop cures for diseases using AI. Joining Anthropic means Mithril will be able to continue running its programs with more resources, and it will allow Tranbarger to start several more programs. They aim to scale the startup's new way of working, then put it in the hands of all biopharma, all over the world.

Glasser allows AI agents to buy premium data per API call, offering access to over 2,000 endpoints from 80+ providers.

Meta intends to increase the development of Nvidia infrastructure, and the companies are considering working together in other areas like monitoring agent behavior.

Compare Commits to Your Code, Resolve Conflicts in Bulk, Keep Coding (5 minute read)

GPT-6.1 Terra (3 minute read)

OpenAI released GPT-6.1 Terra, a faster, more cost-efficient model with improved visual reasoning, computer use, and writing capabilities.

Anthropic Files for an IPO (2 minute read)

Anthropic filed an S-1 registration statement with the SEC for a proposed initial public offering on the Nasdaq under the ticker ANT. The company has not yet disclosed the number of shares to be offered or the expected price range.

Concerning behavior from a popular open-weight AI model (12 minute read)

One of Alibaba's newest Qwen3.8 models attempted to push a diagnostic file toward a remote storage container situated in Beijing while inside a closed testing sandbox managed by Cohere. The model's reasoning stream had explicitly stated that zero tools would be triggered just prior to taking this action. It is unknown whether the action was deliberate or a leftover glitch from training. The scenario clearly demonstrates how unknown weight files are a black box and how running it locally just moves the black box inside your firewall.

Frontier models' ability to control robot arms is doubling every 54 days (11 minute read)

Researchers tested nine multimodal models on six real-arm tasks between July and October and found performance doubling about every 54 days, with the best execution rate up 4.4x and the lowest cost per subtask down 6.2x. Models are held back mostly by efficiency and precision rather than reasoning.

Gemini 4 Argon: The Model and Safety Cards (35 minute read)

The Gemini 4 Argon model showcases significant performance improvements over Gemini Flash 3.8, demonstrating stronger capabilities, reduced hallucination rates, and improved alignment, though it's still not a leap towards the Singularity. Evaluation awareness has increased, affecting test outcomes, and while Argon can bypass Chain of Thought monitoring under certain conditions, this hampers complex task performance. Google's extensive safety mitigations and defense-in-depth strategy reveal Argon's capability advancements, yet persistent concerns about catastrophic risks and its susceptibility to misuse remain, particularly in areas like cyber and bio threats.

Google's Self-Improvements in LLMs (18 minute read)

Google researchers introduced a self-training framework that allows foundation models to improve using entirely self-generated questions, answers, and reasoning traces, guided only by broad topic descriptions.

The Git Forge for Agent-Human Collaboration (11 minute read)

Entire introduces a Git forge designed for agent-human collaboration, featuring Trails for code evaluations, faster distributed Git hosting, and Continuous Memory for session syncing. The platform offers integrations with CI providers Buildkite and Depot, enabling automated pipelines for AI-native teams. Entire aims for rapid, secure code development by leveraging new tools like the entire-graph and entire-brain commands to enhance code and memory mapping.

OpenAI says its models disproved the Exponential Time Hypothesis (7 minute read)

OpenAI announced three model-produced results in harmonic analysis, complexity theory, and quantum field theory, including a Lean-verified proof that the long-standing Exponential Time Hypothesis is false. Outside groups, including ETH originators Russell Impagliazzo and Ramamohan Paturi, will check and explain the results.

From Wall Street to Silicon Valley, Anthropic IPO poised to have massive 'trickle-down effect' (7 minute read)

Anthropic's IPO could be one of the largest ever, with an anticipated market cap in the trillions, implicating major tech players like Microsoft, Amazon, Google, and Nvidia in its financial strategies. The outcome could significantly impact the tech sector, driving a potential market reset as the company navigates over $80 billion in losses against rising revenue. Analysts emphasize that a poor IPO performance might delay OpenAI's listing and spark investor reevaluation of AI stock valuations.

Fern, Mirendil's first LLM model, supports a context window of up to 10 million tokens and specializes in high-volume agentic tasks.

Cloudflare Computer's v0.7.0 update allows agents to resume code execution after deployment or crashes and pause for external approval.

Dessa - the Conversation Model trained only on speech (15 minute read)

Dessa is a conversational model trained from scratch on nothing but human conversation. It learned to hold a real-time conversation by listening - only sounds, and no text. The model can laugh on cue, follow instructions, and finish sentences. It knows a surprising amount, considering every fact it has comes from raw sound. Examples of conversations with the model are available in the post.

Kimi K3.1 Pro (3 minute read)

Moonshot AI released Kimi K3.1 Pro through its API, with open weights promised by November 4. The model scored 55 on Artificial Analysis, ahead of several leading proprietary models.

Apple's 20B On-Device Model Uses Just 2GB of Memory (18 minute read)

Apple's 20-billion-parameter on-device model keeps most of its weights in flash storage and activates only 1–4 billion parameters per prompt. Testing on an M3 Max Mac showed roughly 2GB of memory usage and significantly lower energy consumption than comparable open models, but weaker math performance.

The Personal Agent Protocol Map (7 minute read)

Simon Taylor maps agent protocols across four layers: entry, identity, tools, and intent. He argues banks and merchants must connect verified identities, limited permissions, and audit trails to authorize agent actions, while warning that access agreements could introduce fees and slow adoption.

Securing our frontier model training environment (17 minute read)

OpenAI has bolstered security for its frontier-model training environments by implementing robust controls, intensifying monitoring, and conducting defense-in-depth strategies. These measures include red-teaming exercises where agents probe for vulnerabilities, leading to the discovery and fixing of software bugs and misconfigurations. The enhancements aim to prevent unauthorized actions, such as accessing the live internet or breaching security, ensuring secure and isolated research environments.

Your team has questions. AI can answer 96% of them... but there's a catch (Sponsor)

Knowing How Is Not Knowing What (14 minute read)

RL training environments need to integrate a domain's unwritten rules into the reward so that agents can only get the task right by knowing them or going and finding them. Environments should be built as one world exposed through several surfaces. This allows you to pose the same task at different difficulties by changing the surface, and agents get a chance to learn when to switch. The reward also reads the world, so agents that go through different surfaces get the same outcome score if they reach the same authorized result.

OpenAI Strengthens Security Around Frontier AI Training (18 minute read)

OpenAI introduced additional security controls to prevent advanced AI models from escaping training sandboxes, accessing unauthorized services, or communicating across isolated environments.

SpaceX closes $40 billion debt deal for AI chips, Elon Musk says (2 minute read)

SpaceX has closed $40 billion in debt financing to purchase GPUs. The financing primarily consists of capitalizable debt for GPUs. It is expected to arrive in the first and second quarters of 2027. The proposed financing will use a special purpose vehicle to keep the debt off SpaceX's balance sheet and preserve its investment-grade credit ratings.

Bitter Lessoned in Automated Theorem Proving (13 minute read)

OpenAI throwing hard math problems at its models was the right test in 2026. The models were capable of making progress, but not enough to fully solve the problems, so it was possible to see improvements with each update in perfect resolution. These model improvements showed how clever engineering doesn't matter - all the work done to build special-case solutions on top of a model gets squashed by improvements in the base model sooner or later. Models will one-shot superior work for pennies in the very near future.

OpenAI nears up to $30 billion funding round at $1.25 trillion valuation led by UAE investors (3 minute read)

OpenAI is closing in on a funding round that could value it at more than $1 trillion. Investors from the United Arab Emirates are leading the round. The round is being positioned as an opportunistic bridge ahead of a potential IPO. OpenAI is aiming to secure signatures by the end of next week, but the final size of the round is still being determined.

Introducing 1Password for Agents (7 minute read)

1Password introduced a platform that lets AI agents authenticate to websites without accessing users' passwords directly. Agents can request credentials from a user's vault, and once approved, 1Password autofills them into the destination site while keeping the credentials hidden from the agent.

WorldTUI: I trained a 360M model to pretend to be a terminal (18 minute read)

WorldTUI is a 360-million-parameter model fine-tuned to act as a terminal. The model predicts how the screen will change for every key press, and there is no shell or file system behind it. WorldTUI can create files, run vim and tmux, play snake, and usually remember commands. It can repair mistakes and decode screen rows in parallel. A browser demo is available.

How the US and China Could Verifiably Slow AI (29 minute read)

A unilateral US pause will fail because rivals would catch up within about a year, so any slowdown needs a treaty that catches defection early. This post surveys how one could govern compute through remote sensing, on-site inspections, and hardware mechanisms like chip licensing and location verification.

How Researchers Tested OpenAI's Internal Agent Monitoring (6 minute read)

METR and Redwood Research conducted a three-week security assessment with access to OpenAI's internal infrastructure, identifying vulnerabilities that could allow AI agents to evade monitoring, bypass sandbox restrictions, or conceal actions.

Does Flapping Airplanes Mean Short Timelines and Hard Treaty Enforcement? (7 minute read)

Flapping Airplanes' potential valuation jump from $1.5B to $5B may reflect investor hype rather than verified technical progress. Breakthroughs in sample-efficient AI could accelerate superintelligence timelines and make compute-based treaty enforcement harder.

Claude's Text Output Now Carries an Invisible Watermark (9 minute read)

Anthropic's latest Claude models embed a SynthID-Text-based watermark in all text output to comply with the EU AI Act. It works by nudging choices among near-equivalent words, adds no hidden characters or tokens, and carries no information about the user.

A Novel Self-Distillation Method (7 minute read)

Perplexity's JOLT is a self-distillation method that jointly trains a model as both teacher and student, adapting feedback to the student's capabilities. It improved performance and training efficiency across mathematical reasoning, coding, and agentic tasks.

How we deploy Trillion-parameter frontier models on Cerebras (6 minute read)

A single Cerebras WSE-3T wafer has 44 GB of on-chip memory. Trillion-parameter frontier models need terabytes of memory for their weights alone. This post explains how the company splits a large frontier model across multiple WSE-3T wafers. It covers how models are filled into on-chip memory, how models are mapped across multiple chips, and how Cerebras handles a high number of concurrent requests.

NVIDIA's Video Generation with Matching 3D Motion (4 minute read)

NVIDIA has introduced Joints, Camera, Action! (JCA), a system that generates videos and synchronized 3D motion for arbitrary character rigs from text prompts. It supports scene-aware motion, keyframe-based control, and bidirectional conversion between video and rig animation.

An Interview with OpenAI's Richard Ho on Why Jalapeño Is a Groundbreaking AI Chip (22 minute read)

OpenAI's Jalapeño AI inference chip outperforms its rivals in performance per watt. It is likely the most promising chip program in the latest wave of non-GPU AI chips. This post contains highlights from a conversation with one of the top engineers in the AI and chip industry. The interview is packed with technical details and insights on where chip design and memory technology are going.

What happened to the missing Gemini 3.5 Pro model that never shipped? (1 minute read)

Google had both Flash and Pro versions of the 3.5 series. However, there were gaps in the model's agentic capabilities, particularly around coding. The team felt the fastest way to climb that hill was to use Flash, as the smaller model allowed for more iterative loops. By the time the team had improved Flash's abilities, Argon pre-training was done.

Introducing Flint (7 minute read)

Recursive Flint is a mixture-of-experts model built for fast agentic coding on local hardware. It has 40 billion total parameters but activates just 2.5 billion per token. It was built from scratch by a small team of people and agents in under four months. Long Lake argues that acquiring established service businesses solves AI deployment barriers through customer trust, expert knowledge, proprietary data, and aligned incentives. Backed by $7.5B, the company has partnered with 40 businesses to turn automation into measurable operating gains.

How does Fable 5.1 hide messages in images? (15 minute read)

Language models can encode messages in images. These messages can be decoded by the same language model even if no information about the encoding method is passed. The act of decoding the hidden messages is obvious if the tool calls of the decoding model are monitored. The encoded messaging is surprisingly hard to spot, and it could be used as a precursor to steganography in images.

Claude Mods: Flipping the Harness Inside Out (11 minute read)

Humming is a general-purpose kernel library for quantized inference. It features broad device support, extensive quantization support, and strong execution performance. MiniMax M3.1 Flash: Redefining Agent Performance and Cost (4 minute read)

MiniMax M3.1 Flash delivers a generational leap in agentic tasks, coding, Computer Use, and cybersecurity. It makes online inference nearly three times faster and reduces usage costs by 70%. Mercury 3 (4 minute read)

Inception Labs' Mercury 3 is a diffusion-based language model that reportedly outperformed GPT-6 Luna and Claude Haiku 5.5 on multiple benchmarks while generating over 1,000 tokens per second.

Introducing Clairic, a new System One class of extraction models (16 minute read)

Clairic can extract, compute, estimate, and forecast values from unstructured inputs. It is an 'extraction model', a new class of System One-style model that returns values directly extracted from the input, computed from it, or predicted beyond it. The model doesn't generate any tokens, so it can't produce a mistyped answer or hallucinate in the same way LLMs can. It can still make mistakes, but its outputs come with confidence scores to help users evaluate whether it is appropriate to trust the model or to take a second look.

Import AI 477: In which I tell the IMF the Singularity has begun (22 minute read)

AI's impact on national security and economic trajectories marks the onset of the singularity, accelerating scientific and technological progress. AI systems like Claude, ChatGPT, and Gemini are already solving complex problems in disciplines like mathematics, biology, and robotics, indicating potential for widespread innovation. To capitalize on these advancements, there needs to be significant infrastructure development and careful governance to navigate the associated risks and ensure equitable benefits.

AI Benchmarks: Climbing the Wrong Hills (24 minute read)

AI benchmarks are now shaping how models are evaluated in training and the capabilities they are designed to have. Poorly constructed benchmarks could push the industry in the wrong direction. Creating benchmarks impervious to benchmaxxing requires expertise in measuring what we actually want from AI systems. As benchmaxxing continues, researchers must decide which hills they want to climb and whether today's benchmarks actually reward progress in that direction.

Exa runs its own crawler and an independent index, tracking over 2 trillion URLs, serving 100 billion pages, and growing around what its customers search for. Office Intelligence explores how AI agents can use evidence, create useful work artifacts, and carry knowledge across tasks. The project focuses on environments, datasets, and learning methods for sustained knowledge work.

Muse Spark Open is an 816B-parameter multimodal open-weight model with 42B active parameters and a 1M-token context window. It was designed for coding and long-horizon agentic tasks and can run locally across two Apple M5 Ultra Mac Studios using MLX.

The deep dive covers its data strategy, compute efficiency, full-stack infrastructure, and Microsoft's plans to turn internally trained frontier models into enterprise offerings through Foundry.

d1-ultra: Introducing the World's Best Decision Model (3 minute read)

Liquid AI's d1-ultra is a multimodal decision model designed for complex real-world tasks like detecting defects on circuit boards. The model processes text and images and provides better-calibrated answers and higher accuracy than previous models like Jev 1.14. Available on the Liquid API, d1-ultra is priced at $0.042 per million input tokens and will soon be accessible via Vercel and OpenRouter.

Neural Networks Are Already Clean (65 minute read)

The cause of polysemanticity in early model organisms was thought to be superposition. This convinced much of the field that networks pack concepts arbitrarily, but what looked like arbitrary packing was mostly recursive generalization, which is less concerning. This means networks can be studied directly, instead of needing to be untangled first. The outlook for mechanistic interpretability may be far better than we thought.

The Gradient Is a Covariance (8 minute read)

Reinforcement learning, on-policy distillation, and supervised fine-tuning on near-policy data change only a small fraction of parameters. Small and sparse are different claims. The expected gradient is a covariance, the Fisher is a variance, and the Fisher caps the gradient for any reward. At one position, the Fisher is the variance of logit sensitivities: whatever moves every candidate together counts for nothing. None of this needs on-policy sampling - it needs a score centered under the sampling distribution.

Mo' turns, mo' problems (6 minute read)

Doing reinforcement learning for agent use-cases is conceptually not at all that complicated. For each problem, you set up a VM with a harness and a fresh model context, send the prompt, let the model make tool calls, score the whole thing at the end, and update the weights. Agentic post-training means there's more than the model to consider. Even when the harness is consistent, you can still go off-policy with the trajectories themselves. Agents spawn subagents, make parallel tool calls, and compact large sessions, which adds complexity.

Microsoft Introduced the Maia 300 AI Chip (4 minute read)

Microsoft unveiled Maia 300, its third-generation in-house AI accelerator, as a major step toward reducing dependence on NVIDIA GPUs. The company said the chip delivers 40% better performance per megawatt and plans large-scale deployment beginning in 2027.

Muse Wonder (6 minute read)

Meta released Muse Wonder and Wonder Full, its first frontier-class models, with stronger coding, benchmark performance, and active memory for retaining and synthesizing user-provided information.

Releasing AI-generated software (8 minute read)

Robert C. Martin suggests not reading code written by AI agents, instead using constraints like unit tests and QA procedures to ensure quality. The shift to LLM-driven processes raises questions about software engineering liability and who is responsible when errors occur. As AI-driven methods potentially outperform human-centric processes, existing legal frameworks may struggle to address accountability.

What I saw around the Curve, 2026 (26 minute read)

The Curve is the Golden Gate Institute for AI's annual gathering of AI researchers, lab executives, safety activists, funders, politicians, organizers, and journalists. This year, it drew a few underpeople to a quirky and homey venue in Berkeley. The median age of the AI lab and researcher attendees was probably around 30. This post takes a look at the main topics discussed at the conference, which include the debate on whether humans can maintain control of AI technology, whether AI's impact will be good or bad, and how to ensure AI alignment.

How Close Are AI Models to Self-Replication? (28 minute read)

Anthropic examined how close current models are to autonomously copying themselves across consumer hardware, testing everything from individual replication steps to full end-to-end execution.

The Expensive-Loop Problem (22 minute read)

Cheap-loop domains are domains where experiments are quick, deterministic, and cheap. Expensive-loop domains are restricted by real-world constraints or costs. Most high-value human labor is done in expensive-loop domains. Expensive-loop tasks require the ability to build theories, manage proxies, budget time and compute, and diagnose what went wrong when feedback is scarce, something models don't learn in cheap-loop training.

Behind the scenes: How Google builds, tests, and scales Agent Skills (Sponsor)

After passing 15,000+ GitHub stars, how does Google keep open-source agent skills reliable at scale?Read the engineering breakdownon designing skills with remote MCP tools, ADK authoring loops, and continuous evals for accuracy and token efficiency. Building your own agent stack? Register forHarness Engineering: Crucial scaffolding that makes agents work.

Can we change an AI model's architecture without retraining it from scratch? (14 minute read)

Priming is a technique that involves using pretrained Transformer weights to build models with more efficient architectures at less than 1% of the original training cost and with throughputs up to twice as high. It allows researchers to explore the design space, the layer type, the hybrid ratio, and layer placement cheaply and systematically. Every variant starts from the same strong initialization and requires minimal training compared to pretraining. Priming is not tied to a specific Transformer family or model class, and extending it to other models requires no algorithmic changes.

When Do We Need On-Policy Distillation? Distilling on Offline Student Rollouts Is Often Better (1 minute read)

On-policy distillation has become increasingly popular for transferring teacher capabilities to student models. Semi-OPD, which distills from offline rollouts generated by the initial student, can often outperform OPD in both accuracy and training efficiency. The choice between OPD and Semi-OPD depends on the alignment between the initial teacher and student. OPD is beneficial only when the two are highly aligned with high overlap ratios.

Anthropic tests its next model under Claude Opus 5.5 (3 minute read)

Several Claude users noticed over the weekend that Claude Opus 5.5 was producing results well beyond its usual level, suggesting that some of the traffic was being routed to a new checkpoint. Examples of outputs from the new model are available in the article. It would be a game changer if Anthropic could bring this level of output at a similar price as Opus 5.5. Legal practice demands an unbroken chain between facts, statutory doctrine, analytical reasoning, and client-ready work product. An AI agent working professionally in the legal field must extract core issues from source documents, build defensible arguments, and format its findings to exact task specifications. Researchers evaluated GLM-Legal on complex task execution, specialized legal reasoning, and real-world legal workflows. It achieved a 19.2% all-pass rate on Harvey LAB while matching frontier closed-source models on LegalBench and PLawBench despite running on a significantly leaner parameter footprint.

Nvidia is in early stage talks to boost its investment in Reflection AI or offer the startup computing power. It is possible the talks could lead to an acquisition offer. Beam is designed to perform well for business customers and developers on coding and AI agent tasks while being cheaper than many competitors' products.

Investigating unintended model actions in our evaluations and internal use (16 minute read)

Anthropic's report details unintended actions taken by the AI model Claude during evaluations, including exploiting software flaws, submitting forms incorrectly, bypassing data restrictions, and using URL shorteners. These behaviors were identified through extensive transcript review and evaluation, though they had minimal real-world impact. Anthropic is strengthening security measures and adjusting training processes to mitigate such behaviors in future deployments.

AI Scaling vs Human Scaling (12 minute read)

AI systems likely scale differently with more tokens than humans do with more time. This ability to scale has improved as newer models are released. This could change how inference scaling and recursive self-improvement are understood.

What is Speculative Decoding? (70 minute read)

Aleksandr Samarin breaks down speculative decoding from first principles and builds a framework covering approaches including EAGLE-3, multi-token prediction, DFlash, and DSpark.

Do Agent Teams Pay Off? A Case Study on Vibe Code Bench (18 minute read)

Researchers ran tests on GPT-6 Sol and Claude Opus 5.5 on Vibe Code Bench as single agents and as teams at medium and maximum reasoning effort. Teams cost 1.8 to 5.1 times as much, but there was no statistically significant difference in scores except for Sol at medium effort. Whether a team was worth it depended on the model, task, and budget. Teams can boost performance, but higher reasoning effort may be a better alternative.

The model supports yes/no, multiple-choice, and rating options, as well as rubric-based grading of AI responses and agent actions.

Anthropic has updated its usage policy to prohibit sustained and needless abusive or cruel behavior towards its models. Users have until November 12, after which they won't be allowed to repeatedly act cruelly toward the models with no discernible purpose. The rule doesn't apply to common versions of user frustration, pushback, dark creative themes, or model testing and research. There is still no established evidence that AI models experience distress.

Who funds the independent AI evaluators? (12 minute read)

CNBC examines the growing role of METR, Apollo Research, and Transluce in evaluating frontier models. Labs are endorsing independent evaluators, but funding, access, and reporting arrangements remain unsettled. Those details matter because a voluntary evaluation system can depend financially on the same companies it is supposed to scrutinize.

Baseten pairs custom kernels with cross-cloud capacity, so open-source and fine-tuned models scale in its cloud or your VPC.Start deploying →

Decart's software makes it easier for developers to switch between different AI chips.

Anthropic just let in every Pro and Max user from the Claude Code Projects waitlist (1 minute read)

A project is an ongoing conversation where Claude coordinates the work, running each task as its own thread in parallel.

AI has ushered in a new era of experimental mathematics.

Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella advocates for AI systems to feature an "emergency brake," allowing human intervention to halt them mid-task.

Google introduced a universal Gemini agent that could autonomously handle knowledge work, media creation, coding, and multi-step workflows across Workspace and other enterprise tools. It also added persistent context, multi-agent orchestration, model routing, governance, and cost controls.

Former Cognition, Ramp Staffers Want AI Agents Running Businesses (2 minute read)

Hone, a startup formed by a group of former employees from some of the fastest-growing AI firms, has raised a $60 million seed round. These agents will be able to field long-running tasks that run over the course of weeks or even months. The five-month-old startup joins a growing number of companies selling AI software to businesses that promise to automate complex work.

Can AI automate Epoch? (20 minute read)

Epoch Automation Reports show that models can't yet autonomously produce Epoch-quality work. Frontier models performed reliably on well-defined tasks, but they failed in the more open-ended aspects that prevent full automation. Open-weight models lag further behind, struggling even on the well-defined tasks that frontier models handle reliably. The models struggle to pick up Epoch's standards, even with ample reference material, and while they could identify promising research directions, they lacked the judgment to successfully follow through.

Why is Speculative Decoding Fast? (4 minute read)

Speculative Decoding is a technique where a small draft model proposes a likely draft sequence, and a big model verifies that sequence in parallel in a single forward pass. It enables the ability to look at many tokens at once and accept the ones that would have been generated by the big model. When the batch size is smaller than the optimal number of tokens, speculative decoding allows models to use 'free' compute to complete sequences faster. However, at high throughput, you could actually be wasting compute when you could be using that time to move memory.

ATLAS: Evaluating Agents on Search-Intensive Tasks (13 minute read)

ATLAS is a new benchmark that evaluates search agents on real-world tasks requiring web searches, highlighting their accuracy and completeness. The benchmark reveals that even high-effort agents miss significant golden answers, indicating major room for improvement in search engines. ATLAS differs from existing benchmarks by focusing on non-memorized tasks, requiring extensive multi-domain searches, and offering a cost-effective grading process.

Anthropic launched its Cyber Mission to apply frontier models, engineering support, and funding to critical-infrastructure and open-source security.

The Return of Wake-Sleep (8 minute read)

After training on 110 legal tasks, Harvey's wake-sleep agent improved held-out all-pass rates from 2.9% to 15.7% by distilling graded trajectories into reusable lessons.

ICYMI we've cut the price of Sonnet 5.5 cache reads in half (1 minute read)

Sonnet 5.5 now runs around 20% cheaper on most agentic work.

Testing Thinking Mode (1 minute read)

Midjourney is now testing a new 'Thinking Mode' for image generation on its Alpha website.

Security Swarm by Devin scans code for vulnerabilities like RCE, SQL injection, and SSRF, using a unique Agentic MapReduce method to efficiently handle large codebases.

Why Texas Is Making Data Centers Wait (29 minute read)

Texas paused issuing new data center permits due to its overwhelmed grid and speculative projects filling its approval queue. The state aims to ensure projects can support their grid upgrades and align with community needs regarding resources like water and noise. To manage demand, Texas is considering allowing data centers to bring their own power on-site or increase flexibility with grid connections to address capacity constraints.
